about: Sovereign DAW / SovaRoll task queue. One bounded task at a time; record real evidence.

tasks.title: E2E: audio fade-in/out from Inspector changes the rendered mix
tasks.goal: Prove in the real GUI that setting a fade-in on an audio clip makes the rendered mix quieter at the clip start, and that Undo removes it.
context: Inspector audio clip form (#clip-form) has inputs name="fadeInSeconds" and name="fadeOutSeconds" (rendered in public/app.mjs around line 724).
They are hidden unless the server capability audioClipFades is true (it is true in the current server).
Renderer applies fadeInFrames/fadeOutFrames in src/media/render.mjs; source WAV is never modified.
acceptance: New E2E step(s) in scripts/gui-first-delivery-smoke.mjs, placed after audio.GUI-clip-trim-length: select the first imported audio clip, set fadeInSeconds=0.5, submit, assert project clip fadeInFrames equals 0.5 s in asset frames.

Render via CLI (cli('render', file)) and assert RMS of the first 0.05 s of that clip region is less than half of the RMS at 0.45–0.5 s into the clip (compute on the mono sum (L+R)/2; the MIDI track also sounds at those times, so compare against the same window rendered before the fade was set).
Click #undo and assert fadeInFrames is gone/0, then #redo is NOT required; leave project state consistent for later steps (later steps' expectations must still pass).
Step name: audio.GUI-fade-in-changes-render. Whole E2E still passes.
notes: Do not change product code unless the test reveals a real bug; if it does, record it in the evidence.
tasks.evidence: npm run agent:e2e: E2E PASS, 28 steps including audio.GUI-fade-in-changes-render; fadeInFrames=0.5s in asset frames, before/after CLI mono-sum RMS comparisons, and Undo passed. npm run agent:verify: VERIFY PASS (guard and all .mjs syntax; unit tests skipped because this GUI-smoke-only change has no related unit test file). No product code changed; FD-20 scope limits recorded.

tasks.title: E2E: audio clip mute and polarity invert from Inspector
tasks.goal: Prove clip-level mute removes the clip from the mix and invert polarity flips sample sign, both undoable.
context: #clip-form checkboxes name="audioMute" and name="invertPolarity".
Muted clips render dimmed (class muted-clip on .timeline-clip).
acceptance: Check audioMute on the recorded clip, submit; project clip.mute === true; the .timeline-clip for it has class muted-clip; CLI render RMS over the recorded clip region drops to (near) zero compared to before.
Undo restores mute false.

Check invertPolarity on the imported clip; CLI render sample at a fixed frame inside that clip has opposite sign to the render before (compare with tolerance, other tracks muted via CLI command track.update or measure where only that clip plays).
Undo restores. Step names: audio.GUI-clip-mute-silences-render, audio.GUI-clip-polarity-inverts-render. Whole E2E passes.
tasks.evidence: npm run agent:e2e: E2E PASS, 30 steps including audio.GUI-clip-mute-silences-render and audio.GUI-clip-polarity-inverts-render. Recorded mono-sum RMS 0.0975930279 to 0 after mute; fixed PCM sample -0.1178283691 to +0.1178283691 after polarity inversion; muted-clip state and both Undo paths passed. Initial silent fake-mic baseline was corrected by supplying a deterministic tone WAV; assertions unchanged. npm run agent:verify: VERIFY PASS (guard and syntax; no related unit tests). No product code changed.

tasks.title: E2E: clip normalize button sets clip gain to reach the target peak
tasks.goal: Prove the Inspector 'clip normalize' action (data-action=normalize-audio, target #audio-normalize-target) changes only clip gainDb, is undoable, and leaves the asset file unchanged.
context: Handler: public/app.mjs (search: normalize-audio) → POST /api/audio/normalize → clip.update gainDb.
Imported test tone has peak 0.4 (≈ -7.96 dBFS).
acceptance: Set #audio-normalize-target to -1, click the normalize button for the imported clip; clip gainDb ≈ +6.96 (±0.05).
Asset WAV sha256 unchanged.
Undo restores the previous gainDb. Step name audio.GUI-normalize-sets-clip-gain. Whole E2E passes.
tasks.evidence: npm run agent:e2e: E2E PASS, 31 steps including audio.GUI-normalize-sets-clip-gain. -1 dBFS target set clip gain within 6.96±0.05 dB, all non-gain clip fields deep-equal, source WAV SHA-256 unchanged, Undo restored previous gain. npm run agent:verify: VERIFY PASS (guard and syntax; no related unit tests). No product code changed.

tasks.title: E2E: cycle (locator loop) playback wraps the transport
tasks.goal: Prove that with locators set and #cycle-playback pressed, playback position loops inside the locator range.
context: Locators: CLI command project.locators {range:{startTick,endTick}}; GUI button #cycle-playback runs project.cycle {enabled}.
Preview renders the locator range and loops the AudioBuffer; position display is #position-time / #position-bars.
acceptance: Set locators to bar 1–2 (0..3840 ticks at 4/4) via CLI command, click #cycle-playback, assert project.cycleEnabled === true and aria-pressed=true.
Play; poll #position-time for ~3 s of wall time; every sampled position stays within [0 s, 2 s + 0.15 s] and at least one later sample is smaller than an earlier one (wrap observed).
Stop; toggle cycle off; Undo/redo not required. Step name playback.GUI-cycle-loops-locator-range. Whole E2E passes.
notes: Headless Chrome needs --autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required (already set in the smoke).
tasks.evidence: npm run agent:e2e: E2E PASS, 32 steps including playback.GUI-cycle-loops-locator-range. Locators 0..3840 ticks; cycleEnabled and aria-pressed checked; ~3 seconds of position-time samples stayed within 0..2.15s and a wrap was observed; Stop and Cycle off passed. npm run agent:verify: VERIFY PASS (guard and syntax; no related unit tests). Transport evidence only; no listening claim or product code change.

tasks.title: E2E: keyboard Undo/Redo (Cmd/Ctrl+Z, Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+Z)
tasks.goal: Prove the keyboard shortcuts undo and redo the last edit when focus is not in an input.
context: Handler in public/app.mjs keydown: (metaKey||ctrlKey)&&key 'z' → history.undo / history.redo (shift).
acceptance: After any edit, focus #timeline-scroll, press ControlOrMeta+z → revision increases and the edit is reverted; press ControlOrMeta+Shift+z → re-applied.
Step name project.GUI-keyboard-undo-redo. Whole E2E passes.
tasks.evidence: npm run agent:e2e: E2E PASS, 35 steps including project.GUI-keyboard-undo-redo. With #timeline-scroll focused, ControlOrMeta+Z reverted the CLI track-name edit and increased revision; ControlOrMeta+Shift+Z reapplied it and increased revision. npm run agent:verify: VERIFY PASS (guard and syntax; no related unit tests). No product code changed.

tasks.title: Decide: should a ruler click snap the cursor to the grid?
tasks.blockedReason: Needs a human product decision. Currently clicking the timeline/piano ruler sets the cursor to the exact pointer position (e.g. 7700 ticks instead of 7680), so pasting/importing 'at cursor' lands slightly off-grid. Ask the user whether ruler clicks should follow the Snap setting.

context: public/app.mjs seekRuler(event, scope) (search: async function seekRuler).
acceptance: Human decision recorded in this task's notes before any code change.

context: Audio recording controls are created by public/recording-ui.mjs (host.className='recording-controls'); MIDI recording controls by public/web-midi-input.mjs. Check where each host is inserted in the DOM.
All existing ids (audio-record, audio-record-stop, …) must stay the same because smoke tests use them.
acceptance: Recording controls live inside one <details id="recording-panel">; default closed; the transport row is directly followed by the arrangement when closed.
Smoke scripts that click recording controls open the panel first (update gui-first-delivery-smoke and gui-recording-* with openMenu('recording-panel')).
npm run agent:e2e and both recording smokes pass; screenshot before/after saved to .test-output/.

tasks.title: Long project: preview/export of a project longer than 120 s
tasks.goal: Find out and test what happens when a project is ~150 s long: CLI render must succeed (limit is 600 s); GUI Play must either work or show a clear Korean message — never fail silently.
context: src/media/render-limits.mjs MAX_RENDER_SECONDS=600. Older docs mention a 120 s preview window for the built-in instrument path; verify current behaviour in public/app.mjs play() and src/server.mjs /api/render.
acceptance: New integration test tests/long-project-render-integration.test.mjs: create a project with a MIDI note at 140 s via commands, CLI render succeeds and output frames ≥ 140 s × sampleRate.
Document the GUI behaviour in the evidence; if Play fails silently, add a follow-up task (do not redesign playback here).

context: One fresh-tree publication run timed out at audio-track pan after gain; screenshot showed no HTTP failures.
